text.p: Futures closed at record highs and the cash market ended well-supported as investor confidence grew that the European Union's planned single currency would start on time, traders said.
U.S. retail sale figures for May and revised data for April were seen reducing the chances of a Federal Reserve rate hike in the near future.

The Portuguese bond market is closed on Friday and trade on Monday will be heavily affected by any fresh news about the prospects for the single currency that could emerge ahead of the Amsterdam summit, traders said.
Despite the improved mood, after France had appeared to throw the timetable for monetary union into doubt, traders said that the market remained cautious.
They noted that the financial position of France and Germany, twin pillars of a future single currency, was difficult with both battling to get their budget deficits under control.
"It is not a time for euphoria," said one broker.
Despite the prospects for another good inflation figure in May -- the number will be released on June 17 -- there was no narrowing in the yield curve.
